item.title: A Caution About Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
With the advent of artificial intelligence, the widespread use of social media, and a general lack of proper education, it’s getting harder and harder to tell when someone is accurately representing a vehicle for sale.
Artificial intelligence may even be completely out of touch with things like rudimentary trim tag decoding.
While artificial intelligence can certainly be a great resource for car enthusiasts (regarding do-it-yourself mechanical tasks, for example), it is a dangerous place to be looking around for information about vehicle specifics.

item.title: UH launches free ‘AI for Hawaiʻi’ course for everyone
item.description:
As artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly transforms the workforce and daily life, the University of Hawaiʻi is making AI education available to everyone with a new, free online course designed for the people of Hawaiʻi and beyond.
Artificial Intelligence for Hawaiʻi is an open-access, self-paced course that provides foundational AI knowledge and practical skills while addressing responsible and ethical use through a Hawaiʻi lens.

item.title: The Amazon Service Bezos Nicknamed “Artificial Artificial Intelligence” is Closing for Good
item.description:
# The Amazon Service Bezos Nicknamed “Artificial Artificial Intelligence” is Closing for Good Fatima Gulzar
Sun, September 6, 2026 at 8:21 PM GMT+14 min read
- [AMZN \ -0.15%](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMZN/)
CNBC reported that Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: [AMZN](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMZN)) is shutting down Mechanical Turk, its 21-year-old crowdsourced work platform, effective September 30.
Following an assessment, we've made the decision to close AWS Mechanical Turk." Launched in 2005, the platform matched businesses with workers who completed small digital jobs, known as Human Intelligence Tasks, that typically paid a few cents each, including data labeling, transcription, and surveys. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos famously called it "artificial artificial intelligence."
At its peak, the platform served more than 500,000 workers, but CNBC reported the service had been in decline as competing data-labeling companies drew workers away.
[![The Amazon Service Bezos Nicknamed "Artificial Artificial Intelligence" Is Closing for Good](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///ywAAAAAAQABAAACAUwAOw==)](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/9b4f4e17381f2966d895f674981c433f55cc32e9e9b725ef6b2870f3ca91e1ab/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Finsidermonkey.com%2F226ed9ed0936942adb97f3d56073e411.jpg)
The Amazon Service Bezos Nicknamed "Artificial Artificial Intelligence" Is Closing for Good
### **Bull Case** Amazon.com, Inc. Ending the service allows Amazon to redirect whatever engineering and support resources it still uses toward higher-priority businesses, including AWS's growing AI infrastructure and services.
### **Bear Case** Amazon.com, Inc.
Story Continues
Companies such as Scale AI, Mercor and Prolific have built businesses around supplying human expertise and training data to AI developers, which allows them to capture demand that Mechanical Turk once served.
Amazon also risks losing an opportunity to transform Mechanical Turk instead of abandoning it. By shutting down the service, Amazon gives up that potential avenue for participating directly in the growing market for human-generated AI data.
